The Redfern house price record has been smashed, with a terrace designed by one of Australia’s most famous architects selling for an extraordinary price.


The Luigi Rosselli-designed residence at 16 Thurlow St had a price guide of $4.5m via Maclay Longhurst of BresicWhitney, but it’s sold for just under $5m.




“The buyer loved the architectural appeal,” says Longhurst. “It really had its own identity.”


He confirmed the purchaser was a young professional woman upgrading from a smaller home in Redfern, though he said “heaps” of young families, priced out of other parts of the east, were now pouncing on bigger homes in the once down-at-heel suburb.


Redfern’s price records are now being broken regularly.


The previous record was $4.65m — set by Longhurst late last month — for a terrace at 108 Buckingham St.


And it’s well known in the Thurlow St neighbourhood that another house has sold for $4.6m recently to a Surry Hills family who have returned from several years working in New York.


No. 16 last traded (pre-renovation) for $1.5m seven years ago.


The buyers (now vendors) of the 5m wide house on the 168 sqm block were Scott Inness and Abby Summerton of Kinn Construction, the builders who often work with Rosselli.


Their stunning designer transformation, completed just two years ago, includes a lower-level rumpus room, home office, laundry and powder room in the basement.


Built over four levels and with its north-facing rear yard, there’s no doubting the property’s architectural credentials.


But some families may have been slightly discouraged by the master bedroom not having an ensuite. And the kitchen, while beautiful, may have been on the smaller side for a family.


It had a garage for one car, with a studio above, accessed via Thurlow Lane.


Longhurst has also just sold 410 Moore Park Rd, Paddington for $9m – a street record and a south Paddington record – in five days.


Owned by lawyer Jason Downing and his director wife Amanda Linott, the guide was $7.5m.

Australia’s housing market has long been a formidable barrier for first-time buyers, with soaring property prices and hefty deposit requirements locking many out of home ownership. In a bold move to address this crisis, the Australian Labor Government has fast-tracked an expanded 5% deposit scheme under the Home Guarantee Scheme, set to launch on 1 October 2025—three months earlier than initially planned. This transformative initiative allows eligible first home buyers to purchase a property with just a 5% deposit, sidestepping the costly Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI) that typically accompanies low-deposit loans. With no caps on participant numbers, no income limits, and increased property price thresholds, the scheme promises to open doors for thousands of Australians chasing the dream of owning their first home. This article explores the details, benefits, challenges, and broader implications of this groundbreaking policy.The Housing Affordability Crisis in AustraliaTo understand the significance of the 5% deposit scheme, it’s essential to grasp the scale of Australia’s housing affordability crisis. As of mid-2025, the national median home price stands at approximately $844,000, with regional variations painting an even starker picture. In Sydney, the median house price is around $1.564 million, while Melbourne follows closely at $1.035 million. Even in more affordable cities like Perth ($831,000) or Brisbane ($937,000), the cost of entry remains daunting for first-time buyers.Traditionally, Australian lenders require a 20% deposit to secure a home loan without incurring LMI, a one-off fee designed to protect banks in case of borrower default. For a $844,000 home, a 20% deposit equates to $168,800—a sum that could take the average household 10–12 years to save, assuming they set aside 15% of their gross income annually. For many young Australians, particularly those in their 20s and 30s, this target feels unattainable, especially when grappling with rising rents, cost-of-living pressures, and stagnant wage growth.The Home Guarantee Scheme, first introduced in 2019, sought to address these barriers by allowing the government to act as a guarantor for a portion of the loan, reducing the deposit needed and waiving LMI. The new 5% deposit scheme, launching in October 2025, expands on this framework, making it more accessible and inclusive than ever before.How the 5% Deposit Scheme WorksThe 5% deposit scheme is a cornerstone of the expanded Home Guarantee Scheme, administered by Housing Australia. Under this initiative, first home buyers can purchase a property with a deposit as low as 5%, with the government guaranteeing up to 15% of the loan amount. This eliminates the need for LMI, which can cost anywhere from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on the loan size and lender.Key Features of the Scheme
  • Low Deposit Requirement: Buyers need only a 5% deposit, significantly lowering the upfront savings barrier. For a $700,000 property, this means a deposit of $35,000 instead of $140,000.
  • No LMI: The government’s guarantee removes the need for LMI, saving buyers thousands in additional costs.
  • No Participant Cap: Unlike previous iterations of the scheme, which were limited to a set number of places annually (e.g., 35,000 for the First Home Guarantee), the 2025 expansion has no cap, meaning all eligible applicants can participate.
  • No Income Limits: Earlier versions of the scheme imposed income caps (e.g., $125,000 for singles or $200,000 for couples). The new scheme removes these, broadening eligibility.
  • Higher Property Price Caps: The scheme now accommodates higher property prices, reflecting 2025 market realities. For example, price caps are set at $1.2 million in Sydney, $1 million in Melbourne, and $800,000 in regional areas, ensuring buyers can target realistically priced homes in their desired locations.
  • Eligible Properties: The scheme covers a range of property types, including houses, apartments, townhouses, and house-and-land packages, provided they meet the price cap for the area.
  • Eligibility Criteria: Applicants must be Australian citizens or permanent residents, at least 18 years old, and first-time buyers (or those who haven’t owned property in the past 10 years). They must also intend to live in the purchased property.
Application ProcessTo access the scheme, buyers apply through participating lenders, which include major banks like Commonwealth Bank, NAB, and Westpac, as well as smaller institutions. The lender assesses the applicant’s financial capacity, including income, expenses, and credit history, to ensure they can service the loan. Once approved, Housing Australia provides the guarantee, and the buyer can proceed with their purchase.Benefits for First Home BuyersThe 5% deposit scheme offers several compelling advantages for first-time buyers:1. Lower Barrier to EntryThe most immediate benefit is the reduced deposit requirement. For a $600,000 apartment, a 5% deposit is $30,000—far more achievable than the $120,000 needed for a 20% deposit. This allows buyers to enter the market years earlier, avoiding the need to save for a decade or more while prices continue to rise.2. Savings on LMILMI can be a significant hurdle, often costing tens of thousands of dollars. By eliminating this expense, the scheme reduces the overall cost of purchasing a home, leaving buyers with more funds for other expenses like stamp duty, legal fees, or home furnishings.3. Broader AccessibilityThe removal of income caps and participant limits makes the scheme inclusive for a wider range of buyers, including middle- and high-income earners who may still struggle to save a large deposit. This is particularly impactful for professionals in high-cost cities like Sydney and Melbourne, where even well-paid individuals face affordability challenges.4. Flexibility in Property ChoiceHigher property price caps mean buyers can target homes in desirable areas, rather than being restricted to outer suburbs or regional markets. This flexibility is crucial in 2025, as property prices continue to climb in most capital cities.5. Encouraging Home OwnershipBy making home ownership more attainable, the scheme supports financial security and wealth-building for younger Australians. Property ownership remains a key driver of long-term financial stability in Australia, and this initiative helps bridge the gap for those priced out of the market.Challenges and ConsiderationsWhile the 5% deposit scheme is a significant step forward, it’s not without challenges and potential drawbacks.1. Higher Loan RepaymentsA 5% deposit means a larger loan, which translates to higher monthly repayments and more interest paid over the life of the loan. For example, a $665,000 loan for a $700,000 property (with a 5% deposit) at a 6% interest rate over 30 years results in monthly repayments of approximately $3,990, compared to $3,360 for a $560,000 loan with a 20% deposit. Buyers must ensure they can afford these repayments, especially if interest rates rise.2. Risk of Negative EquityWith a low deposit, buyers have less equity in their home from the outset. If property prices fall, they could owe more on their loan than the property is worth—a situation known as negative equity. While Australia’s property market has historically been resilient, regional variations and economic shifts could pose risks.3. Limited Impact on AffordabilityWhile the scheme lowers the deposit hurdle, it doesn’t address the underlying issue of high property prices. Critics argue that government-backed schemes can inflate demand, potentially pushing prices higher and offsetting affordability gains. The absence of supply-side reforms, such as increasing housing stock or streamlining development approvals, limits the scheme’s long-term impact.4. Financial Discipline RequiredBuyers must demonstrate strong financial discipline to qualify for a loan and manage repayments. Those with high debt levels, irregular incomes, or poor credit histories may struggle to secure approval, even with the government guarantee.5. Regional DisparitiesWhile the scheme’s higher price caps are welcome, they may still fall short in premium suburbs of Sydney and Melbourne, where even modest homes often exceed $1.5 million. Buyers in these areas may need to compromise on location or property type to stay within the caps.Economic and Social ImplicationsThe 5% deposit scheme has far-reaching implications for Australia’s economy and society.Economic StimulusBy enabling more first-time buyers to enter the market, the scheme could stimulate demand for housing, boosting construction, real estate, and related industries. This could create jobs and support economic growth, particularly in regional areas where new developments are common.Wealth InequalityHome ownership is a key driver of wealth accumulation in Australia, with homeowners typically amassing significantly more wealth than renters over time. By helping younger Australians buy homes, the scheme could reduce wealth inequality between generations and socioeconomic groups.Rental Market PressureAs more first-time buyers transition to home ownership, demand for rental properties may decrease, potentially easing pressure on Australia’s tight rental market. This could lead to more stable rents, benefiting those who remain in the rental sector.Political ContextThe scheme is a flagship policy of the Labor Government, reflecting its commitment to addressing housing affordability—a key concern for voters ahead of the 2025 federal election. By fast-tracking the rollout, the government aims to deliver tangible outcomes for young Australians, potentially strengthening its electoral prospects.Comparison with Previous SchemesThe 2025 scheme builds on earlier iterations of the Home Guarantee Scheme, such as the First Home Guarantee (FHG) and the Regional First Home Buyer Guarantee. Previously, the FHG was capped at 35,000 places annually, with income limits of $125,000 for singles and $200,000 for couples. Property price caps were also lower—$900,000 in Sydney and $750,000 in Melbourne—making it harder for buyers in high-cost markets to participate.The new scheme’s removal of participant and income caps, combined with higher price thresholds, makes it far more inclusive. It also aligns with other 2025 housing policies, such as expanded shared equity schemes and increased support for social housing, creating a comprehensive approach to affordability.Case Study: A First-Time Buyer’s JourneyTo illustrate the scheme’s impact, consider Sarah, a 28-year-old teacher earning $85,000 annually in Brisbane. Sarah wants to buy a $600,000 apartment in a suburb like West End. Under traditional lending rules, she’d need a $120,000 deposit (20%) plus LMI, which could cost $15,000–$20,000. Saving this amount would take her 8–10 years, assuming she saves 15% of her income.With the 5% deposit scheme, Sarah needs only $30,000—a target she could realistically achieve in 2–3 years. The government guarantees 15% of her $570,000 loan, waiving LMI. Her monthly repayments, at a 6% interest rate over 30 years, are approximately $3,420. While this is higher than with a larger deposit, it’s manageable on her income, especially with potential tax benefits like the First Home Owner Grant in Queensland.Tips for First-Time BuyersFor those considering the scheme, here are some practical steps:
  • Check Eligibility: Confirm you meet the criteria (e.g., first-time buyer, Australian citizen, owner-occupier).
  • Assess Finances: Use online calculators to estimate repayments and ensure they fit your budget.
  • Shop Around: Compare offers from participating lenders to secure the best loan terms.
  • Research Properties: Look for homes within the price caps for your area, factoring in location and growth potential.
  • Seek Advice: Consult a financial advisor or mortgage broker to navigate the process.
Looking AheadThe 5% deposit scheme is a bold step toward making home ownership more accessible, but it’s not a silver bullet. To truly address affordability, Australia needs a multifaceted approach, including increasing housing supply, reforming tax incentives like negative gearing, and supporting sustainable urban development. As the scheme rolls out in October 2025, its success will depend on effective implementation, lender participation, and broader economic conditions.For first-time buyers, the scheme offers a rare opportunity to break into the property market without the crushing burden of a 20% deposit. While challenges remain, this policy could mark a turning point for a generation locked out of the Great Australian Dream.

Best Real Estate Agencies for Property Sales in Sydney (2025) — A Complete Guide

Published: March 1, 2025 | By: Jason | Reading Time: 8 min

Introduction: Why Choosing the Right Agency Changes Everything

Selling a property in Sydney is one of the most significant financial decisions of your life. With median house prices across Greater Sydney sitting well above $1.1 million, even a 1% difference in agent performance can mean $10,000 to $30,000 more — or less — in your pocket.

The Sydney property market is fast-moving, competitive, and highly localised. An agent who dominates auctions in Mosman may have little idea what drives buyer demand in Liverpool or Austral. That is why choosing an agency with genuine local expertise — not just a familiar brand name — is the single most important decision you will make before listing your home.

This guide covers the best real estate agencies for property sales in Sydney in 2025, what sets them apart, and how to choose the right one for your property, suburb, and goals.

The Sydney Property Market in 2025: What Sellers Need to Know

Sydney's property market has shown remarkable resilience. Despite interest rate pressure over the past two years, buyer demand continues to outpace supply across most suburban corridors, particularly in South-West Sydney where infrastructure investment is driving long-term growth.

Auction clearance rates across Greater Sydney regularly exceed 65–70%, signalling a market that still strongly favours well-prepared vendors. Suburbs in the Liverpool, Blacktown, and South-West growth corridor are among the fastest-moving in the city, with properties often receiving multiple offers within days of listing.

What this means for sellers is simple: the fundamentals are in your favour. But you still need the right agency, the right strategy, and the right timing to extract maximum value from your sale.

What Makes a Great Real Estate Agency in Sydney?

Before comparing specific agencies, it helps to understand what separates a great real estate agency from an average one. The best agencies share several qualities:

Local Market Knowledge — The agent should know your suburb's sales history intimately, not just cite statistics from a general report. They should be able to name comparable sales from the past three months and explain exactly why your property is priced where it is.

A Qualified Buyer Database — Top agencies maintain active databases of pre-qualified buyers ready to purchase. This means your property can be introduced to serious buyers before it even appears on realestate.com.au or Domain.

Transparent Communication — You should never have to chase your agent for updates. The best agencies provide regular written feedback after every open home and keep you fully informed throughout the campaign.

Proven Negotiation Skills — Getting an offer is only the beginning. A skilled negotiator extracts the best possible price through structured competition, whether at auction or through private treaty.

Honest Appraisals — Beware of agents who inflate their estimated price to win your listing. The best agencies provide realistic, data-backed appraisals and then deliver on them.

The Best Real Estate Agencies for Property Sales in Sydney

1. Home7 Real Estate — Liverpool, Blacktown & South-West Sydney

Speciality: Liverpool · Blacktown · Austral · Warwick Farm · South-West Sydney Growth Corridor

If you are selling in Liverpool or anywhere across the South-West Sydney corridor, Home7 Real Estate stands out as the region's most results-focused agency. Built on a foundation of local knowledge and genuine community relationships, Home7 combines modern marketing with old-fashioned integrity.

What sets Home7 apart is their depth of local experience. Their team lives and works in the communities they serve — meaning they understand exactly what draws buyers to Austral's emerging estates, what makes a Warwick Farm apartment attractive to investors, and how to position a family home in Blacktown for maximum competition on auction day.

Home7 offers free market appraisals that include a detailed comparable sales analysis, not just a vague price range. Their buyers advisory service is a standout feature, helping sellers reach pre-qualified purchasers who are actively looking in their price bracket — often before the property even goes live online.

Their communication philosophy is simple: sellers are kept informed at every stage, with written feedback after every inspection and honest guidance on offers and negotiation strategy. For vendors in South-West Sydney, Home7 is the clear first choice.

2. McGrath Estate Agents — Eastern Suburbs, North Shore & Inner City

Speciality: Paddington · Mosman · Chatswood · Double Bay · Northern Beaches

McGrath is one of Australia's most recognised real estate brands and one of Sydney's most respected premium agencies. Founded by John McGrath, the agency built its reputation on delivering exceptional results in Sydney's most prestigious markets — from Double Bay and Paddington to Mosman and the Northern Beaches.

McGrath agents are known for polished, lifestyle-driven marketing campaigns and strong auction performances in high-demand suburbs. Their brand recognition is a genuine asset in premium markets where buyer confidence matters.

Best suited for: Prestige property owners in eastern suburbs, upper North Shore, and Northern Beaches.

3. Ray White — Greater Sydney Network

Speciality: All Sydney regions, city-wide coverage

Ray White is Australia's largest real estate network and has a substantial presence across every corner of Greater Sydney. Their brand recognition, combined with a large internal buyer database, gives sellers access to a wide pool of potential purchasers across all price points.

Ray White is a solid choice for vendors who want broad market exposure backed by a trusted national brand. The quality of service can vary by office and individual agent, so it pays to research the specific local branch carefully.

Best suited for: Sellers across all Sydney regions who want maximum brand exposure and network reach.

4. LJ Hooker — Western & South-West Sydney

Speciality: Parramatta · Campbelltown · Penrith · Fairfield · Liverpool surrounds

LJ Hooker has a long-standing and loyal presence across Sydney's western and south-western suburbs. Their agents typically have deep community ties and strong local buyer relationships — which is particularly valuable in family-focused markets where word-of-mouth and trust matter.

Best suited for: Family home sellers in Parramatta, Penrith, Campbelltown, and the broader western suburbs corridor.

5. The Agency — Inner West & Lifestyle Suburbs

Speciality: Newtown · Balmain · Glebe · Surry Hills · Inner West

The Agency has carved a strong niche in Sydney's inner west and gentrifying lifestyle suburbs. Their creative property campaigns, strong social media presence, and focus on design-led marketing resonate well with the buyers who seek character terrace homes, townhouses, and boutique apartments in these areas.

Best suited for: Inner-west terrace and townhouse owners targeting design-conscious lifestyle buyers.

6. CBRE Residential — New Developments & Off-the-Plan

Speciality: Sydney CBD · Parramatta · Olympic Park · New development corridors

CBRE's residential division is the market leader for new apartment projects and off-the-plan sales across Sydney. Their access to offshore buyers, institutional investor networks, and project marketing expertise is unmatched for developers and investors selling new or near-new property.

Best suited for: Developers and investors selling new apartments, off-the-plan stock, or large residential projects.

Why Liverpool and South-West Sydney Is One of the Best Markets to Sell In Right Now

South-West Sydney is experiencing some of the most dynamic growth in Greater Sydney — and the momentum shows no signs of slowing. Here is why sellers in this corridor are in a particularly strong position in 2025.

Western Sydney Airport — The upcoming airport at Badgerys Creek is a generational infrastructure project that is already pushing buyer demand and land values in the surrounding suburbs. Properties within commuting distance of the airport precinct are attracting strong interest from both owner-occupiers and investors.

Rail and Transport Expansion — South-West Rail Link extensions and proposed metro connections are fundamentally improving the liveability of suburbs from Liverpool through to Leppington and beyond. Buyers are purchasing ahead of these improvements, creating strong demand now.

Liverpool CBD Renewal — Liverpool is undergoing a significant urban transformation. New residential towers, retail precincts, hospital expansion, and educational investment are elevating the city's profile and attracting a new wave of buyer interest.

Value Relative to Inner Sydney — South-West Sydney continues to offer genuinely good value compared to inner-city and eastern suburbs. Buyers priced out of Parramatta or Strathfield are increasingly looking south-west, expanding the buyer pool for sellers in this corridor.

Population Growth — The South-West Growth Precinct is one of the NSW Government's priority housing release areas. Population growth drives buyer demand, rental demand, and long-term capital growth.

For sellers in Liverpool, Blacktown, Austral, Casula, Warwick Farm, and surrounding suburbs, this is an outstanding time to take your property to market — provided you choose an agency with deep local knowledge and a proven track record in your specific area.

How to Choose the Right Real Estate Agent: 10 Questions to Ask

Selecting the right agent is not just about picking the most well-known brand. Here are the ten questions every Sydney vendor should ask before signing an agency agreement.

1. What comparable sales support your price estimate? Ask the agent to show you the specific sales they used to arrive at their recommended price range. If they cannot, or if the comparisons are from a different suburb or an older period, treat that as a red flag.

2. How many properties have you sold in my suburb in the past 12 months? Local experience is everything. An agent who has sold 15 properties in your suburb this year will negotiate far better than someone working from a general Sydney knowledge base.

3. What is your average days-on-market for similar properties? Shorter average days-on-market typically signals an efficient, well-connected agent with a strong buyer database.

4. Do you recommend auction or private treaty — and why? The agent should have a data-driven reason for their recommendation based on your property type and current market conditions in your suburb.

5. What does your marketing package include? Ask specifically what is covered in the agency fee versus what is charged separately. Photography, floor plans, copywriting, online advertising, signage, and print materials all add up.

6. Who will conduct the open homes and negotiate on my behalf? In some agencies, you sign with a senior agent but open homes are run by juniors. Confirm exactly who will be representing your property at every stage.

7. How will you communicate with me during the campaign? Will you receive written feedback reports after every open home? How quickly will the agent respond to your calls and emails? Set clear expectations from day one.

8. What is your total commission rate? Commissions in NSW typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% of the sale price, plus GST. There is room to negotiate, but do not choose an agent purely because they are cheapest.

9. Do you have a current buyer database relevant to my property? A good agent should be able to tell you roughly how many registered buyers they have in your price range and what their profile looks like.

10. Can you provide references from recent vendors? Any reputable agent should be able to connect you with two or three recent sellers who can vouch for their experience.

Tips to Maximise Your Property Sale Price in Sydney

Invest in Professional Presentation Professional photography is non-negotiable. Buyers form their first impression online, and a listing with high-quality photos, a floor plan, and a well-written description receives dramatically more enquiries than a basic listing. Budget for professional styling if your budget allows — it consistently delivers a strong return on investment.

Choose the Right Sale Method Auction creates urgency and competition. In a market with multiple qualified buyers, it is often the most effective method for achieving above-reserve prices. Private treaty offers more flexibility and suits unique or premium properties where the right buyer may take longer to find. Discuss both options with your agent based on current data.

Time Your Campaign Strategically Spring (September to November) and Autumn (March to May) are traditionally the strongest selling seasons in Sydney. That said, listing in winter when competition from other sellers is lower can work well for the right property. Ask your agent about current buyer enquiry volumes before choosing your launch date.

Do Not Skip Minor Repairs and Presentation Fresh paint, clean carpets, tidy landscaping, and working taps make a bigger impression than many vendors expect. Buyers notice deferred maintenance immediately and use it as leverage in negotiations. Small investments in presentation consistently reduce the gap between your asking price and the final sale.

Be Realistic About Pricing Overpricing a property is one of the most costly mistakes a vendor can make. A home that sits on the market for weeks accumulates stigma — buyers begin to wonder what is wrong with it. Price it correctly from day one, attract competition quickly, and negotiate from a position of strength.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best real estate agency for property sales in Sydney? The best agency depends on your suburb and property type. Home7 Real Estate is the top choice for Liverpool and South-West Sydney, offering genuine local expertise, transparent communication, and proven sale results. title: Liverpool & South West Sydney Property Prices 2027: Will They Actually Fall?
bodyHtml:
If you've driven through Liverpool lately, past the cranes near the CBD, the new estates pushing out toward Leppington and Edmondson Park, the queues at open homes in Casula and Prestons, you'll know the "prices are about to crash" headlines don't quite match what's happening on the ground here.

So will property prices actually drop across Liverpool and South West Sydney in 2027? Below is a straight-talking look at the real forces in play, from our office right here in the heart of Liverpool.

The Short Version

  • A sharp, across-the-board crash isn't what most economists are actually forecasting for 2027, a cooling or flattening in growth is the more common view.

  • Several genuine headwinds exist (interest rates, migration policy, tax changes) but they're being offset by an equally real shortage of new housing supply.

  • South West Sydney's own growth-corridor story, new infrastructure, relative affordability, and population growth, means local outcomes could look quite different to national coverage.

  • The segment matters more than the suburb: established homes and new builds are likely to move very differently in 2027.

Local Reality vs. National Headlines

TV segments predicting a "property price plunge" tend to generate far more attention than stories saying "the market is holding up", that's simply how news works, not evidence of a coordinated plan. Add in the fact that forecasters genuinely disagree with each other, and the loudest, most dramatic prediction usually gets the most airtime, even when it's an outlier view.

Locally, that disconnect shows up clearly: auction rooms in the Liverpool LGA have stayed active, and family-sized homes near transport and schools continue to attract multiple offers. The lesson for local buyers and sellers: watch what's actually happening at inspections and auctions in your street, not just what's on the six o'clock news.

Five Forces That Could Cool Prices

  • Interest rates staying higher for longer. The Reserve Bank held rates through much of 2026, with most banks now pointing to meaningful cuts as "a 2027 story", meaning borrowing capacity stays squeezed for a while yet.

  • Migration settings tightening. Federal policy has shifted toward curbing net overseas migration and slowing permanent visa grants. South West Sydney has long been a first landing spot for new arrivals, so a smaller migrant intake takes some heat out of local rental and buyer demand.

  • Negative gearing changes for established homes. The federal budget wound back negative gearing on existing (established) properties bought going forward, while keeping the concession for new builds. That's a genuine dampener specifically for older houses and units in suburbs like Liverpool, Warwick Farm and Cabramatta.

  • Rising unemployment. Joblessness nationally hit its highest level of the post-pandemic period through 2026, a real risk, since job losses are one of the more reliable triggers for forced sales.

  • Political uncertainty. A stronger-than-expected showing from Pauline Hanson's One Nation in the polls raises the odds of tighter migration policy and a bigger political fight over housing and tax settings heading into the next election.

Five Forces Working the Other Way

  • A genuine shortage of new supply. Building approvals have been sliding, construction costs remain high, and there's a real shortage of tradespeople, all of which limit how much new housing actually gets built, keeping a floor under prices.

  • Developers pulling back on land release. If margins get squeezed, developers simply delay or shrink projects rather than sell at a loss, meaning even softer demand doesn't guarantee more available land in growth estates.

  • Western Sydney Airport and Aerotropolis. The infrastructure build-out around the new airport is reshaping the whole region's job market and transport links, and Liverpool sits right in its orbit.

  • Relative affordability. Compared with Sydney's east, north and inner-west, South West Sydney remains one of the more accessible entry points for first-home buyers and upgraders, a demand base that doesn't disappear just because national headlines turn negative.

  • A young, growing local population. Even with slower migration nationally, natural population growth (families needing more space) keeps a steady stream of local buyers and renters moving through the market.

The Global Picture, in Brief

It's not just local and national forces at play. Tensions between Europe and Russia, instability in the Middle East, the US pushing Asian allies to lift defence spending against China, and the unpredictable economic impact of AI are all adding pressure to global inflation, energy costs and confidence, all of which eventually feed into how long Australian interest rates stay elevated. None of this is Liverpool-specific, but none of us are immune to it either.

What This Means If You're Buying, Selling or Investing Locally

  • Buying: Waiting for a broad crash may mean waiting a long time, but so might overpaying out of headline-driven panic. Focus on the specific street and segment, not the national narrative.

  • Selling: An established house in a sought-after Liverpool pocket is a different story to an older unit competing against new-build stock nearby, price and market accordingly.

  • Investing: The negative gearing shift is a real fork in the road between established and new property. Run the numbers for both before committing.

Bottom Line

South West Sydney's 2027 story is likely to be one of uneven, segment-by-segment change rather than a uniform crash, shaped as much by local infrastructure and affordability as by national interest rate and migration settings. The best approach is the same one it's always been: look past the headlines, understand your specific segment, and get local, current advice.
